text:
Jenny (Sales): heads-up — ACME legal sent back the SIG + CAIQ, they flagged KMS/HSM questions. need a concise answer for the redline by EOD.
Alex (Security): OK, can you paste the specific questions?
Jenny (Sales): main asks: at-rest encryption details, BYOK options, HSM attestation, key rotation policy, and whether we support external KMS (customer-managed). they want an explicit statement for the contract.
Maria (Solutions): short answer: we encrypt data at rest with AES-256 using envelope encryption; root keys can be in our managed KMS or the customer's KMS via BYOK. we support HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3) for Dedicated and Private deployments.
Tyler (Infra): implementation notes for POC: for Private/VPC we can integrate with customer KMS via standard KMIP/Cloud KMS APIs or by importing wrapping keys. For Hosted, we offer a BYOK flow where customer uploads a wrapping key via KMS integration (no plaintext keys stored).
Alex (Security): add controls: key usage logging, access via IAM roles, HSM attestation certs available on request, and monthly rotation recommendations. also mention envelope encryption and key hierarchy so we don't expose data keys.
Jenny (Sales): can we specify rotation cadence options for the legal team? they asked for "key rotation frequency and who enforces".
Maria (Solutions): recommend defaults: data key rotation: automatic per-object rewrap as needed (no change to app), wrapping key rotation: 90 days recommended for high-sensitivity customers, 365 days for standard. Customer can enforce via their KMS if BYOK. Add: automated rollovers use dual-write period to avoid outages.
Tyler (Infra): POC steps to demonstrate: 1) create dedicated VPC POC, 2) enable KMS integration with test key in customer project, 3) run sample workload and show logs/metrics, 4) export signed attestation + HSM cert chain. I can provision the infra if Sasha confirms timings.
Sasha (Customer): we prefer HSM-backed keys and want to see attestation + CA certs. timeline: earliest next Wed for POC start.
Alex (Security): for contract wording sample: "All data at rest is protected with AES-256-GCM using envelope encryption. Customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported via standard KMS integrations; HSM-backed keys meet FIPS 140-2/3 requirements. Key rotation policies can be configured by the customer or follow Redwood defaults (wrapping key: 90–365 days). Access to key material is restricted to authorized personnel and logged for audit."
Jenny (Sales): perfect. can we also add a snippet about in-transit encryption and egress controls? they asked about TLS and whether we ever send keys offsite.
Alex (Security): add: all traffic to/from our endpoints uses TLS 1.2+ (we prefer TLS 1.3) with strong ciphers; customer keys are never exported from the KMS in plaintext and we do not transmit raw key material outside of the configured KMS integration.
Maria (Solutions): include a short code/example for the BYOK flow so they can see it's standard:
```bash
# Example: check key exists in customer KMS before POC
aws kms describe-key --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-efgh
# We then configure Redwood with the key ARN and a wrapping policy.
```
Jenny (Sales): I'm going to paste Alex's contract snippet + Maria's POC steps into the CAIQ response. Sasha — can you confirm Wed next week works?
Sasha (Customer): Wed works. thanks, team. one ask — can we get the HSM attestation pdf before the call?
Tyler (Infra): will generate attestation and upload to secure S3 link (signed). posting link in thread when ready.
SecBot: attestation-upload: file uploaded to https://redwood-secure.s3/attestations/acme-poc-attestation.pdf (access: ACL=private, expires in 7d) :lock: :white_check_mark:
Jenny (Sales): sending to legal now. cc @Alex (Security) for any follow-ups. :thumbsup:
